clue.text: Humbert Humbert's clasping part of hand

indicators.note: the doubled name holds the wanted letters in its grip, across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Humbert Humbert, narrator of Nabokov's Lolita, is holding a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clasping' tells you the name holds the answer: humberT HUMBert.
explanation.definitionFit: The digit set apart from the four fingers is a part of the hand.

clue.text: See 14
Family member for whom Napoleon spied?

definitions.meaning: Napoleon Solo was the agent in the TV series The Man from ....

explanation.surface: A relative for whom Napoleon Bonaparte did a spot of espionage.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon is not the emperor but Napoleon Solo, spy hero of the 1960s TV show The Man from U.N.C.L.E.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative: your parent's brother, and also the spy agency in the old TV series.

clue.text: Migrant rhetoric? Must be Tories/NF, I suspect

indicators.note: used as an adjective, suspect letters are dodgy and not to be trusted in their present order

explanation.surface: A speaker suspects that anti-migrant talk comes from the Conservatives or the National Front.
explanation.walkthrough: NF is the National Front, a British far-right party; Tories are Conservatives. 'suspect' is the anagram signal on MUSTBETORIESNFI.
explanation.definitionFit: Political talk about migrants claiming welfare: the charge that people move country to collect state handouts.

clue.text: Aus. opener bats for "the other side", according to Farage

indicators.note: bats in the sense of crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An Australian opening batsman bats for the opposition, as Nigel Farage would put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like cricket, but means crazy: rearrange AUSOPENER. Nigel Farage is the British Brexit campaigner who cast the continent as the opposing side.
explanation.definitionFit: To a Brexiteer, people of the mainland continent are the opposing side.

clue.text: Stitches ruined Totti's last Rome derby

indicators.note: a ruined thing is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt
last here picks the final letter of the footballer's name

explanation.surface: Footballer Francesco Totti's final Rome derby was spoilt by stitches from an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totti's last' gives I; 'ruined' rearranges I plus ROMEDERBY.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative needlework is made of ornamental stitches.

clue.text: Little Richard made a stack

definitions.meaning: a short, familiar form of the name Richard
a haystack or similar pile of hay or corn

explanation.surface: The rock and roll singer Little Richard built a pile of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Richard is not the singer: read it as a shortened Richard. 'made' just links the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A diminutive of a man's name, and an old word for a haystack.

clue.text: Review of papers cancelled by agreement in 8?

definitions.text: Review of papers cancelled by agreement in 8?

parts.words: Review of papers cancelled by agreement in 8?
parts.note: the agreement signed at the Luxembourg village of 8 removed checks of travel documents at internal borders

explanation.surface: An academic paper review is called off by some deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Papers are identity documents, not academic ones; the agreement named after 8 scrapped border checks between member states.
explanation.definitionFit: The checking of travellers' documents at a border, which the Schengen deal abolished between signatories.

clue.text: Drivers protect golf range

indicators.note: the drivers' letters wrap round and shield the other letter

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British drivers' organisation
G is golf in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Motorists guard a golf driving range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protect' puts G inside AA. A range here is a kitchen stove, and the Aga is a British heavy cast-iron cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large cooking stove, and the Aga is a well-known make of one.

clue.text: Somewhere in Luxembourg, Engineering school leads by two points

indicators.note: the school's letters go in front of the engineering letters

parts.note: ENG is short for engineering
E and N are two compass points

explanation.surface: An engineering school is winning a contest by two points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' are compass points, not a score. The Luxembourg village gave its name to the 1985 agreement on border-free travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A village on the Moselle in Luxembourg where the border-free travel agreement was signed.

clue.text: Reckless, perhaps, for one to have left bird behind

definitions.meaning: Mark Reckless, the MP who quit the Conservatives for UKIP in 2014, is a former Tory

definitions.text: for one to have left bird behind
definitions.meaning: bird is slang for prison time, so a released prisoner has left it behind

explanation.surface: A careless person has left a pet bird behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Reckless is a surname: Mark Reckless defected from the Conservative party, so he is a former Con. Bird is British slang for a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A former Conservative, and a former convict who has served time.

clue.text: Left-leaning character supports the whip

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a lash is a whip

explanation.surface: A left-wing figure supports the party whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left-leaning' looks political but describes a typed symbol that slants to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: The keyboard symbol that slopes from top left to bottom right is literally a leaning character.

clue.text: One falling off the twig, having croaked

definitions.text: One falling off the twig, having croaked

parts.words: One falling off the twig, having croaked
parts.note: falling off the twig and croaking both mean dying, but here an amphibian that croaks falls from a branch

explanation.surface: Someone has died: they have fallen off their perch and croaked.
explanation.walkthrough: Both phrases are slang for dying, but read literally they describe an arboreal amphibian croaking and slipping off a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing amphibian that lives in trees and croaks, so it could well fall off a twig.

clue.text: Poles accept thrust of what's being said

indicators.note: the two pole letters take in the other piece between them

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
to poke is to thrust

explanation.surface: Polish people take in the gist of what someone is saying.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles are not Polish people but the poles S and N, which 'accept' POKE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Words uttered aloud are said, so the past participle means being said.

clue.text: Jack King (revolting Welshman)

parts.note: K is king in chess and cards

indicators.note: revolting as in turning over, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Evan is a typical Welsh man's name

explanation.surface: A king and a rebellious Welshman, as in a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' turns EVAN into NAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pack of cards the jack is also called by an old word for a rogue.

clue.text: Mark's death warrant?

parts.note: the Deutsche Mark was killed off by the single currency agreed in this 1992 pact

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark has been sentenced to death.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark is the German currency: the 1992 European Union agreement set up the euro, which replaced it.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1992 European Union founding agreement that paved the way for the euro and the end of national currencies.

clue.text: Having 12 passionately, relegate first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter is shifted to the end of the word

parts.note: to relegate is to demote

explanation.surface: Someone who spoke with passion demotes the first-placed team to last.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is SPOKEN; 'first to last' sends the D of DEMOTE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to express feeling theatrically, so this is having talked with exaggerated passion.

clue.text: The Girl From Ipanema? Bellissima!

indicators.note: the girl's name is taken from inside the next two words

explanation.surface: Praise for the song The Girl From Ipanema: most beautiful!
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' picks the letters out of ipaneMA BELlissima.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Serbia — a terrible place for fighters

indicators.note: the letters are in a terrible state and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Serbia, war-torn in the 1990s, was an awful place for soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' shuffles SERBIA plus A. Fighters are fighter planes, not soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A military airfield is where fighter jets are stationed.

clue.text: Democrat gripped by terror; it's a global problem

indicators.note: the democrat letters are held inside the terror

parts.note: panic is terror

explanation.surface: A US Democrat seized by fear: a worldwide worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripped by' makes the Democrat the inner piece, held by the terror.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease outbreak across the world is a problem on a global scale.

clue.text: Judge a bishop pinched something from the snack bar

indicators.note: the bishop's letters squeeze the snack between them

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
a bite is a snack

explanation.surface: A judge says a bishop stole food from the café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinched' looks like stealing, but means RR grips BITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone appointed to settle a dispute acts as a judge.

clue.text: Venerated Daily Mail editor's changed sides

indicators.note: the letters at the two ends swap places

parts.note: Paul Dacre was long the editor of the Daily Mail, a British tabloid; the 's gives S

explanation.surface: The once-revered editor of the Daily Mail has switched political allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed sides' swaps the end letters D and S of DACRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held holy is venerated.

clue.text: By gum, we should get rid of this English football manager

definitions.text: By gum, we should get rid of this

parts.note: Tony Pulis is a Welsh football manager known for Stoke and Crystal Palace

explanation.surface: A northern exclamation, By gum!, calling for the sacking of an England football manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By gum' is a northern English exclamation, but here it means beside the gums.
explanation.definitionFit: A benign swelling on the gum, which a dentist would remove.

clue.text: In Colorado, Lou Reed found the blues

indicators.note: the wanted letters sit in the run of the next words

explanation.surface: The rock singer Lou Reed discovered blues music in Colorado.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points inside coloraDO LOU Reed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow and grief, as a feeling of having the blues.

clue.text: Heeds the call of time?

parts.note: in British pubs the landlord calls 'time' at closing and drinkers finish their glasses

explanation.surface: Someone obeys the summons of passing time, or mortality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time!' is the British pub landlord's closing-time call, at which drinkers finish off.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing off one's glass is what a drinker does on hearing that the bar is closing.

clue.text: With this, for open all hours?

definitions.text: With this, for open all hours?

parts.words: With this, for open all hours?
parts.note: this entry's number is 24, and 24 with this word makes the phrase for round-the-clock opening

explanation.surface: An enquiry about a shop that never closes, perhaps the British sitcom Open All Hours.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's own number, 24, joined to the answer gives 24/7, meaning always open.
explanation.definitionFit: The number of days in a week, paired with 24 hours, means non-stop opening.

clue.text: For a bet, TV presenters ignored Washington

indicators.note: those letters are left out and passed over

parts.note: Ant and Dec are a British television presenting duo
DC, the District of Columbia, is Washington

explanation.surface: For a wager, the TV hosts snubbed the US capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a pair of British TV hosts; 'ignored' drops DC from ANTDEC.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker stake put in before the deal is a bet.

clue.text: Eimi scans puzzle having champion quality

indicators.note: to puzzle letters is to jumble them up

explanation.surface: Eimi, editor of the Independent crossword, checks a puzzle that is a winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puzzle' rearranges EIMISCANS. Eimi is the Independent's crossword editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a messiah, a saviour or champion figure.

clue.text: Total wrestling rules nothing out

indicators.note: the round letter is put out of the wrestling word

parts.note: sumo is the Japanese style and code of wrestling
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Wrestling's rules rule out nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes O from SUMO.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the sum of figures added together.

clue.text: Competitor in interstate match?

indicators.note: the versus letter goes inside the pair of states

parts.note: two US states side by side: RI is Rhode Island and AL is Alabama
V for versus, as in a fixture between two sides

explanation.surface: A player taking part in a game between two American states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interstate' is literal: two state abbreviations, with the match's V for versus placed 'in' between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent contesting the same prize as another.

clue.text: Big cheese Mr T became perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Did the A-Team actor Mr T become an important person?
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges MRTBECAME. Big cheese, usually a boss, is here taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft French round cheese, and a fairly sizeable one.

clue.text: Lots of sausages left at the Oktoberfest

definitions.meaning: sausages joined in a chain are sold in strings
the German word for left, as heard at the Munich beer festival

explanation.surface: Many sausages remained uneaten at the Munich beer festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oktoberfest signals German, where the word means left.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausages in a string, and the German for left.
